days.title: When Species Disappear
days.learning_objective: Extinction removes species from Earth permanently.
learning_objectives: Identify and describe the different types of galaxies (spiral, elliptical, irregular).
Explain the formation and evolution of galaxies.
Describe the role of gravity and dark matter in galaxy formation and structure.

days.title: What It Takes to Last
days.learning_objective: Understanding what it takes to last reveals about our world.
learning_objectives: Identify the Milky Way galaxy as our home galaxy.
Describe the basic structure of the Milky Way galaxy (spiral arms, bulge, halo).
Explain the approximate number of stars contained within the Milky Way.
Locate the approximate position of our solar system within the Milky Way galaxy.

days.title: Fitting the Environment
days.learning_objective: Fitting the Environment is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Define a black hole and its key properties (event horizon, singularity).
Explain how black holes are formed from massive stars.
Describe the effects of a black hole's gravity on surrounding matter and light.

days.title: Knowledge You're Born With
days.learning_objective: Knowledge You're Born With is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Identify atoms as the basic building blocks of matter.
Describe the basic structure of an atom, including protons, neutrons, and electrons.
Explain how atoms combine to form molecules and compounds.

days.title: How Your Brain Changes
days.learning_objective: The brain changes and adapts throughout life through neuroplasticity.
learning_objectives: Identify that molecules are formed when atoms bond together.
Provide examples of common molecules and their constituent atoms.
Explain the role of molecules in creating different substances.

days.title: Helping Others Understand
days.learning_objective: Helping Others Understand is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Identify and describe the four states of matter: solid, liquid, gas, and plasma.
Explain the properties of each state of matter in terms of particle arrangement and movement.
Demonstrate the phase changes between states of matter through experimentation and observation.

days.title: How Packed Things Are
days.learning_objective: Understanding how packed things are helps us make sense of the world.
learning_objectives: Define density and explain its relationship to mass and volume.
Calculate density using the formula: Density = Mass / Volume.
Predict whether an object will float or sink based on its density relative to a fluid.

days.title: Force Spread Over Area
days.learning_objective: Pressure is force distributed across a surface area.
learning_objectives: Explain buoyancy as an upward force exerted by a fluid.
Predict whether an object will float or sink based on its density.
Design and conduct an experiment to test buoyancy principles.

days.title: Pushes and Pulls
days.learning_objective: Pushes and Pulls is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Define friction and explain its role in opposing motion.
Identify different types of friction (static, sliding, rolling, fluid).
Describe real-world examples where friction is helpful and harmful.

days.title: How Things Move
days.learning_objective: Understanding how things move helps us make sense of the world.
learning_objectives: Define motion as a change in position over time.
Identify examples of motion in everyday life.
Differentiate between different types of motion (e.g., linear, circular).
Explain how forces affect the motion of objects.

days.title: How Fast Things Go
days.learning_objective: Understanding how fast things go helps us make sense of the world.
learning_objectives: Define speed as the measure of how fast something moves.
Calculate speed using the formula: Speed = Distance / Time.
Identify different factors that affect the speed of an object.

days.title: Speeding Up and Slowing Down
days.learning_objective: Acceleration is the rate of change in speed.
learning_objectives: Define acceleration as the rate of change of velocity.
Calculate acceleration using the formula: a = (vf - vi) / t.
Differentiate between positive, negative, and zero acceleration.
Apply the concept of acceleration to real-world scenarios.

days.title: What Slows Things Down
days.learning_objective: Understanding what slows things down reveals about our world.
learning_objectives: Define force as a push or pull.
Identify examples of different types of forces (gravity, friction, applied force).
Predict how force will affect the motion of an object.

days.title: Why Things Float
days.learning_objective: Understanding why things float matters to us and the world.
learning_objectives: Define momentum as the product of mass and velocity.
Calculate momentum using the formula p = mv.
Explain how momentum is conserved in a closed system.

days.title: How Things Stay in the Air
days.learning_objective: Air is a mixture of gases that surrounds Earth.
learning_objectives: Define inertia and its relationship to mass.
Explain Newton's First Law of Motion.
Identify real-world examples of inertia in action.

days.title: Moving Through Water
days.learning_objective: Water is essential for all life and exists in three states.
learning_objectives: Identify and define the three classes of levers.
Explain how levers multiply force to make work easier.
Calculate the mechanical advantage of a lever system.

days.title: The Human Superpower
days.learning_objective: Human Superpower plays an important role in how the world works.
learning_objectives: Define what a pulley is and its primary function.
Identify different types of pulleys (fixed, movable, combination).
Explain how pulleys change the direction of force and/or multiply force.
Calculate the mechanical advantage of simple pulley systems.
Build and test a functional pulley system using everyday materials.

days.title: Going Up
days.learning_objective: Going Up is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to define 'wheel and axle' and identify its components.
Students will be able to explain how wheels and axles reduce friction.
Students will be able to provide examples of wheels and axles in everyday life.

days.title: Making Structures
days.learning_objective: Making Structures is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Define an inclined plane and explain its purpose.
Demonstrate how an inclined plane reduces the required force to move an object.
Calculate the mechanical advantage of an inclined plane using distance and height.
Identify real-world examples of inclined planes and their applications.

days.title: When Things Come Apart
days.learning_objective: Decomposition breaks matter into simpler components.
learning_objectives: Define a wedge as a simple machine.
Identify at least five examples of wedges used in everyday life.
Explain how the shape of a wedge affects its force.
Design and build a simple model utilizing a wedge.

days.title: Using Things Again
days.learning_objective: Recycling transforms waste into new useful materials.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to define a screw as a simple machine.
Students will be able to explain how a screw converts rotational motion to linear motion.
Students will be able to identify at least three real-world applications of screws.

days.title: When Stuff Ends Up Wrong
days.learning_objective: Understanding when stuff ends up wrong shaped history and our lives.
learning_objectives: Identify different types of gears (spur, bevel, worm).
Explain how gears transfer rotational force.
Calculate gear ratios and their effect on speed and torque.
Design and build a simple gear system to achieve a specific outcome.

days.title: Protecting What We Have
days.learning_objective: Protecting What We Have is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Define the concept of potential energy in relation to springs.
Explain how springs store and release energy through compression and extension.
Identify at least three real-world applications of springs.

days.title: Living Without Using Up
days.learning_objective: Living Without Using Up is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Identify the parts of a pendulum and their functions.
Explain how pendulum length affects the period of oscillation.
Predict the motion of a pendulum based on its starting conditions.

days.title: Weather Patterns Over Time
days.learning_objective: Time passes at a constant rate, yet feels different in different moments.
learning_objectives: Identify the components of a simple circuit (battery, wires, bulb).
Construct a working circuit and explain the path of electricity.
Distinguish between open and closed circuits and their effects.

days.title: What's Happening in the Sky
days.learning_objective: What's Happening in the Sky is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Identify batteries as a source of stored chemical energy.
Explain the basic process of how a battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy.
Recognize common uses of batteries in everyday life.

days.title: The Air Around Earth
days.learning_objective: Air is a mixture of gases that surrounds Earth.
learning_objectives: Identify the colors present in the light spectrum.
Explain how white light is composed of different colors.
Demonstrate how prisms separate white light into its constituent colors.

days.title: Earth's Sunscreen
days.learning_objective: Earth's Sunscreen is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Identify that white light is composed of different colors.
Explain how a prism separates white light into a spectrum.
Describe the concept of refraction and its role in light separation.

days.title: How Plants Eat Sunlight
days.learning_objective: Photosynthesis converts sunlight into food for plants.
learning_objectives: Define what a lens is and explain its basic function.
Differentiate between convex and concave lenses and describe their properties.
Identify real-world applications of lenses in various technologies and everyday objects.

days.title: How Bodies Make Energy
days.learning_objective: Energy transforms from one form to another but never disappears.
learning_objectives: Explain how mirrors reflect light to create images.
Identify different types of mirrors and their uses.
Demonstrate an understanding of reflection through hands-on experiments.

days.title: Blood's Endless Journey
days.learning_objective: Blood carries oxygen and nutrients to every cell in the body.
learning_objectives: Explain how cameras use light to create images.
Identify the key components of a camera and their functions.
Describe the history of photography and its impact on society.
